feature: Fix a caption one word at a time
summary: Double-click one wrong word in a caption, on the picture or on its chip in the Words lane, and you type over just that word. On the Words lane a chip drags earlier or later and carries the words after it, and its edges stretch it. A right-click on a word splits, merges, deletes or moves it.
setup: Photonz Probe, release Next, no flag changed from its default. Open a recording with somebody talking in it and let the captions write themselves.

try.do: Put the playhead in a caption and double-click one wrong word on the picture.
Type the right word and press Return.
Double-click a word's chip in the Words lane under the Captions track.
Type a fix and press Tab: the word is kept and the next word opens. Escape closes it.
Drag a word chip earlier: the words after it come too, and the word before gives way.
Drag the right edge of a line's last chip to stretch that word alone.
Shift-drag a chip to carry every later line too; Command-drag to move one word alone.
Right-click a chip, or a word on the picture, and try Split Here, then Merge with Next.

evaluate: Is a double-click on the picture the first place you would go to fix a misspelled word, and does the field sit where your eye already is?
When you drag a word earlier, is squeezing the word before it what you expected, or should the drag stop at it?
Is Tab to the next word enough to fix a run of typos without the mouse?
At Fit zoom most chips are too narrow for a whole word. Is zooming in (2x, 4x) to read them acceptable, or should the lane show the words some other way?
Does the fold arrow before Captions, which hides the Words lane, earn its place?
rough: Side by side with pages/video-captions.html (Caption track, Words lane): the chips, 26 pt lane, 20 pt chip, 9.5 pt type, lit word in the accent and the Words label match. The mock letters every chip because its words are a second wide. On a 17 second talk at Fit most chips are about 20 pt, so the short ones show two letters and an ellipsis and the shortest show none. Zoom in to read them.
The mock's lit chip is a soft accent gradient. Ours is flat accent, as it was before this change.
The mock has faint second gridlines through the Words lane. Ours has none.
There is no readout while a chip is dragged. You judge the drag by the chips and by the picture, which both follow the hand.
A double-click on the caption's box but off every word still opens the whole line, as before. The line's bar on the track does too.
A fix survives Write Again when the same word is heard the same way at the same moment. A fix made by merging two words does not survive, because the recogniser hears them as two again.

Measured on the probe: the field on the picture opens in 2.4 ms. On the lane the main thread's longest pass for the double-click was 15 ms. Letting go of a drag cost 18 ms, and undoing one 46 ms at worst.
